name: Philip
title: One of the Twelve
tagline: From Bethsaida; the one who told Nathanael, “Come and see.”
story: One of the Twelve, from Bethsaida; Jesus found him and called him, and Philip brought Nathanael to meet Jesus.

periods.title: With Jesus

entries.title: Of Bethsaida
entries.text: “Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter” (John 1:44); John calls it “Bethsaida of Galilee” (John 12:21).

entries.title: No family named
entries.text: Scripture names no family for Philip the apostle.

entries.title: Married, says Clement
entries.text: Clement of Alexandria (about 200), quoted by Eusebius, counts Philip among the apostles who married: “Peter and Philip begat children; and Philip also gave his daughters in marriage.” Polycrates (about 190) speaks of Philip’s “two aged virgin daughters” at Hierapolis and “another daughter” who rests at Ephesus.

entries.title: Greeks come to him: “Sir, we would see Jesus”

h.title: The desire of some Greeks to see Jesus puzzles the disciples and leads Jesus in agitation of soul to interpret life and death as sacrifice and to show how by being "lifted up" he will draw all men to him
The farewell discourse to his disciples in the upper room

entries.title: In the upper room
entries.text: He is named fifth among the Eleven in the upper room (Acts 1:13). Acts never names the apostle again.

entries.title: Papias, as reported by Eusebius (3.39.9)
entries.text: Papias, “their contemporary”, heard “a wonderful tale from the daughters of Philip”; Eusebius says “Philip the apostle dwelt at Hierapolis with his daughters”.

entries.title: Polycrates, bishop of Ephesus, quoted by Eusebius (3.31.3; 5.24.2)
entries.text: “Philip, one of the twelve apostles, who sleeps in Hierapolis, and his two aged virgin daughters, and another daughter who lived in the Holy Spirit and now rests at Ephesus”.

places.name: Hierapolis
places.note: Polycrates (about 190) says “Philip, one of the twelve apostles” sleeps here; the city is named in Scripture only at Colossians 4:13

claim.text: From the same town (John 1:44). With Andrew he brings the Greeks’ request to Jesus (John 12:22), and both speak up before the feeding of the five thousand (John 6:7–8).
In the lists of Matthew, Mark and Luke Bartholomew is named straight after Philip (Matt 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:14).

views.label: The apostle
views.holders: Polycrates of Ephesus (about 190); Clement of Alexandria (about 200)

argument.text: Polycrates calls him “Philip, one of the twelve apostles”, with daughters. Clement names Philip with Peter among the married apostles.

views.label: The household of Philip the evangelist

argument.text: Proclus speaks of “four prophetesses, the daughters of Philip” at Hierapolis. Acts gives Philip the evangelist “four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy” (Acts 21:8–9). Eusebius sets the two reports side by side without comment.

items.from: The identifications this page relies on

argument.text: Three other men called Philip appear in the New Testament: Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven (Acts 6:5; 21:8), Philip the tetrarch (Luke 3:1), and Herodias’s husband Philip (Mark 6:17). This page is about the apostle.

items.q: Did the apostle preach in Samaria?
items.from: The identifications this page relies on

argument.text: The Philip who preached in Samaria and baptized the Ethiopian (Acts 8:5–40) is taken to be the evangelist, not the apostle: the believers were scattered “except the apostles” (Acts 8:1), “the apostles which were at Jerusalem” sent Peter and John to his converts (Acts 8:14), and Acts leaves him at Caesarea (Acts 8:40), where Philip the evangelist lives in Acts 21:8.

items.from: How the story ends: Scripture beside tradition, never blended

items.q: Scripture gives no trade, no family and no later life for Philip the apostle.
Matthew, Mark and Luke name him only in the lists of the Twelve.
Acts 21:8 calls the Philip of Caesarea “the evangelist, which was one of the seven”; Acts 8 does not say which Philip preached in Samaria, though its details point to the same man.
